steps.content: Ever since you came back from the college, not a day has passed that you weren't restless. You haven't so much as accepted Isomer's offer, and already the weight of it has poisoned most of your good spirits.
You open your terminal to browse the college forum, and even there, word of her manages to find you.

Pixel:
Aaaand that's a wrap on the tour! Now, time to flip this table and spill the real tea. Let's talk Isomer and Lambert, shall we? Once upon a time, there was a mentor and his star pupil. Flash forward to now... tsk tsk. A full-blown dumpster fire.

csiaogjra1:
You clout-chasing paper-peddling piece of ****. Piss off. Your account's got 20 minutes, MAX, and that's generous.

Pixel:
Ooooh, now that's so mean! Okay, fine, I hype. I hustle. I sell papers. But everything this lady slings is 100% certified, baby! And just so you little United University keyboard warriors can't scream "fake news" in my mentions, I came strapped with a full package of evidence—

Project Name: City-State-Class Black Ring Catastrophe Dynamic Observation System
Responsible Unit: Catastrophe Defense Engineering Center, Ring Research Institute
Project Leader: Lambert

Pixel:
Of course, Lambert was the original project leader. Our girl Isomer? Buried at the very bottom of the member list. And btw, I've got proof. This Isomer got slapped with a three-rank demotion for a major incident. She was THIS close to being kicked out of the college for good.

Pixel:
THEN, plot twist! Some big shot backed her research and handed her a golden ladder. Isomer stepped over the old Director. Haha... who knows how much she pocketed?

Pixel:
And the personnel records? Oh, they made it sound so classy, alright: <color=#fb9259>Lambert reassigned to consulting advisor.</color> Real translation? Access revoked. Hush-money pension. Entire project handed over. Didn't even leave her old mentor a crumb. Whole Ring Research Institute was dead silent. Hehe... what were they gonna do? She'd already crowned herself Director by then.

Pixel:
Welp, posting all this is def gonna paint another target on my back. Good thing I've got a whole stash of burner accounts this time tho! <color=#fb9259>Master-tier ghostwriting, humanities or sciences! Data fudging, experiment fabrication. 24/7, full-spectrum academic support!</color> Oh, and here's a lil' freebie: swing by that room next to the east wing restroom. Old Lambert'll be right there, sweeping floors every single day.

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: We're both adults here. We've been through enough. Surely we're past clinging to naive ideals and keeping our hands clean?

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: Then, consider my proposal, Chief ${PlayerName}. It's the best chance you'll have. Don't waste it.

The mere memory of her words ties a painful knot in your chest. You shove your terminal aside, drained. And of course, the terminal rings right then. You haul yourself over, fish it back out, and press answer.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Hello? ...Yeah, got it. I'll be right there!
Just like that, the gloom lifts. You roll up, shrug on your coat, and step out.
[Scene Change: Central Library] After you recount everything.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: So... Not only did you meet Isomer in person, but the entire core team at the Observation Hub as well. You confirmed EDGE-07's identity... and even received a covert invitation to collaborate.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Your little excursion turned out far more eventful than I ever imagined. Something straight out of an adventure novel. If I wrote this into a history book exactly as it happened, I'm afraid I'd be accused of wild exaggeration.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Aren't adventure novels supposed to be more romantic than this? This trip was an eye-opener. I never expected the infighting among scientists to rival anything in politics.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: I'm sorry it wasn't what you hoped for. Academia has never been pure. Science and politics, interests, power... they've always been tangled together. Especially in an era like ours, defined by catastrophe.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Right now, Aurum Secretum, catastrophe weapons, and new mines are all under intense scrutiny. They're tied directly to economic production and survival, not to mention commercial rivalries and city-state strategy. Who's to say which breakthrough might upend everything and reshape the world?

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Which is why every sector's been pouring in investment, placing their bets. And the scientists who control those technologies rise right along with the tide. Once that happens... well, things get rather complicated.

steps.speaker: Option
options: Is our history professor feeling a little envious?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I've seen pure scholars who are thrown into the circus of fame, eventually losing themselves among all the temptations. What do you make of that, Professor?
Celine smiles.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: I respect them. Reaching that level isn't as wonderful as you'd expect. History is littered with prominent scientists who were kidnapped, or assassinated.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: You might ask your good friend, General Augustus. Back during the Independence War, who ranked higher on the assassination hit list—her, or the EDGE scholar who provided her with technical support.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Sigh... Knowing the general, she'd probably say, "My reputation strikes too much fear. No one would dare. I'll be generous and let the bald scientist in the back take the top spot this time."
Celine lets out a soft chuckle before lowering her gaze.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: At this stage of civilization, a technological breakthrough can no longer be chalked up to the efforts of a few brilliant individuals. It's part of something far larger, a massive system. Often the key piece of it.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Resources, information, time, talent... it takes the combined strength of entire city-states, of all humanity, really. And you have to navigate something far more complex: human nature. Those pure, idealistic scholars of a bygone era would find it hard to adapt, I think.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Being able to shut yourself away in an ivory tower and pour everything into your research... that's a luxury in itself.
She heaves a sigh, sadness pooling in her expression.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: But I'd be lying if I said I wasn't a little envious. Just look across the way. The College of Science draws students in droves, year after year. Their halls are always buzzing. Meanwhile, our students keep switching tracks. Now, we've only got Linda left, barely holding on with a threadbare budget... It does get lonely, you know.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Sigh... If only you could do a little promoting for us, Chief. A few recommendations here and there.
...Well, when she puts it like that, it really is a little heartbreaking.

You picture the Ring Research Institute's sprawling, splendid architecture, the extravagant banquet spreads at their seminars, and the sheer hum of activity over there. Meanwhile, Linda is left with nothing but study rooms borrowed from the library. The College of Humanities has sunk to renting out its own classrooms to outside groups.
She says her seniors, juniors, and even the faculty keep jumping ship. It honestly gets more depressing the longer you think about it.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I've got to give it to Linda for sticking it out through all of this. You know, she told me that she envies the College of Science too.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Said if she had their resources, their leverage, their connections, a little room to operate in the grey, she'd trade like crazy. Swap favors, cut deals, whatever it took to get her hands on unpublished historical records. Write the hell out of some papers.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: She really is your student, sharp as a tack... and that kind of passion isn't something you can fake.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: She said all that? Hehe, thank you, Chief. You have a real gift for lifting someone's spirits.
She looks genuinely happy now. Perhaps, while the moment is right—

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Then how about returning the favor, Professor? I could use a little cheering up myself. Your colleagues over at the College of Science are giving me a splitting headache.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: How deep do the waters run at the Ring Research Institute, really? What are all these factions actually fighting over? Is there anyone I can even trust? And this whole EDGE-07 situation... should I really get involved? How much risk am I taking, throwing in with a careerist like that? I'm completely in the dark here.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: They say history grants wisdom. Well, I could really use some of yours right now.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: I see... I'm honored that you'd come to me with this. Truly, it makes me happy.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Intelligence, experience, whatever I have that might help, I'm more than glad to share it with you.
For all the tenderness in her voice, she only reaches out with that knowing smile. You recognize the gesture at once. It seems the hour has come for yet another "trade."

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Alright then, let's trade. What are you in the mood for this time?

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Hmm... intriguing. I've read through all the official battle reports, of course. But I could use some personal perspectives to fill in the gaps. Those friends of yours... General Augustus, the Commander-in-Chief, and that Sinner girl who ventured deep into the Outlands. They're all such fascinating subjects.
Jump

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Oh, that's a good one. A rare lens to look through. The Greatest Variable in the N.F. Chronology, The Shifting Status of Sinners, Regional Sinner Communities and Their Social Contexts: A Comparative Study, Daily Life at the Bureau. All excellent topics.
Jump

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: The expedition... I did notice you left out certain details in the DisSea operation reports. If you'd be willing to let me in on it, I'd love that. Just tell it to me as a story. I also have a few friends who are very keen to hear more about the pioneers' exploits.
end

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Thank you for being so generous, Chief.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Now, regarding Isomer and the Ring Research Institute's past, my preliminary findings are ready. Connect to <color=#fb9259>Terminal 0490</color> here in the library, and you can download everything safely with no trace. I've already opened the access for you. Any future updates, you can sync at your convenience.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Though I suspect these materials won't resolve what's really troubling you. They won't answer the questions you're actually facing right now.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Neither can I.
You go still. The questions rise to your lips, only to be halted by her smile.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: But...

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: So... Why don't we take a break, and you can hear about what I found instead?

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Thanks to the doors you opened, my West District fieldwork turned out to be quite productive. The recordings and photos alone are nearly filling up my storage, and I'm still sorting through everything. Come, join me. Who knows? You might even be able to fill in a few gaps for me while we're at it, Chief.
She presses play with a radiant smile. Before long, familiar voices reach your ears.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: You want to talk about Rustfire? Ah, you really know your stuff! Whoever sent you my way, what an eye for talent, what impeccable judgment! I am, without question, the single most devoted witness to that glorious, heart-wrenching chapter of history.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: And not just Rustfire! From the West District to DisCity to the world beyond, from BR-002 to the golden age to the N.F. Chronology! Long, grueling, magnificent, tragic! I couldn't possibly do it all justice in one sitting, but...

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: I've composed 108 new epic poems celebrating this radiant era! Not just my own hand, mind you, but collaborative works with the future blossoms of West District! You must include them all in your history book! I hereby grant you full rights!

steps.speaker: Crache
steps.content: How about you learn a thing or two from her first? You know, proper research methodology, maybe some effective teaching techniques? Then see if you can borrow her library card while you're at it. You've been drooling over that collection for years, and this professor here happens to be its head librarian.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: Crache! Impeccable timing. Look! I've included that assignment you handed in last time among the 108 poems! You too shall be immortalized alongside the rest of us!

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: Ooh, ooh, me too! I know stuff about outside the city, way, way farther than WhiteSands! I just got back, in fact! There's this insanely awesome scientist over in Fraser, like, my age, and she's a total freakin' genius!

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: Oh, and I can tell you all about my adventures too! All the... what's that word again? Right! Local customs. And culture. Let's start with Tuco!

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: I've verified the list of people you proposed to visit, ma'am. Some of them have already passed away. We can try reaching out to their family, or... hm...

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: If you really wish to learn about the individuals themselves, and you wouldn't be averse to unconventional approaches... I happen to know two "specialists" who might be able to offer some leads.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: There are also a few people with rather sensitive statuses. Nirvana has been stirring up trouble nonstop, so it's not safe for them to show themselves. You won't be able to meet them directly, but...

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: If Chief were to accompany you, I believe we could still arrange something. Some of them have been missing their old friend, after all.

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: Shush! Don't go saying it out loud! I'm not looking to get nabbed just yet! Can't we just... sneak a little meeting? Make it look like we bumped into each other, you know? A surprise! A happy coincidence!

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: Ahem! Well, hey there, handsome! You look awfully familiar. Spitting image of an old buddy of mine, actually. How about we grab some skewers? They do amazing barbecue in the satellite town!
steps.female_content: Ahem! Well, hey there, gorgeous! You look awfully familiar. Spitting image of an old friend of mine, actually. How about we grab some skewers? They do amazing barbecue in the satellite town!

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: It was truly an unforgettable experience. I met the hero of legend and made the acquaintance of a teacher from the Syndicate Academy, who turns out to be a journalist and poet as well. She shared so many fascinating stories with me. The kind you'd never find in any newspaper.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: And then there are Romanesque's two leaders. Heh... This is the first time I've collected "echoes of the dead" as historical source material. I still don't know how to analyze something like that.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You might want to take some of what you heard with a grain of salt. Especially Raven's, uh... "literary creations."

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Of course. Organizing the materials, extracting the information, discerning each narrator's subjective lens, and finally distilling a truth one can stand behind... that's the fundamental competency of any chronicler worth their title.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: But for me, the greatest reward was crossing that divide between East and West. Walking down streets I'd only ever seen in photographs. Meeting the people who actually live there. At first, they were wary of a "Paradeisos scholar" like me, and curious, too. But by the end of each conversation... every one of them shook my hand.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Words, in the end, can only hold fragments. The real history has settled into every brick and stone of West District, into the people whose lives are woven into that place. When they opened their hearts to me... that's when I truly saw the marks time had left behind. And the light still shining through them, too...
Her gaze drifts somewhere far away. It's a long while before she draws it back and lets it settle on you again.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: I can imagine how much you treasure them. And I can guess, at least a little, how difficult it must be for you in circles like these... The calculations, the maneuvering, the impossibility of reading anyone's true intentions. You're not at ease here, are you?

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: I can't make your choices for you. The advice and intelligence I offer are just one more voice in the noise. One perspective among many. I'm glad you trust me, but in the fog of an age like ours, you're the one who must ultimately tell truth from falsehood.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: It's not so hard, really. Sometimes you just need to set aside the reports and summaries other people have compiled. Step out of the study. Go see and hear for yourself, up close. The way you took me to the West District.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: As long as you know what you truly want, and you're clear on which lines you will never cross, I believe you can keep moving forward. You'll be able to walk whatever road that leads you down.
As she speaks, your gaze falls upon the book she's handed you. It remains there, fixed, for a long while.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...You're right. I think I do know what I want.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Then that's enough. Look into your own heart. And make your choice.

You remotely access Terminal 0490 once more and sync the materials Celine has provided. She's given you a basic overview of the internal dynamics at the Ring Research Institute, a detailed record of Isomer's promotions, as well as a list of projects she's been tied to since assuming the directorship.

An appended note reads: *Materials incomplete. For reference only.* Still, it is more than enough to keep you occupied for a good while. To be frank, you'd much rather see a few lines of Celine's own commentary on the woman. Sadly, the history professor clearly had no intention of leaning one way or the other on this matter, so you'll just have to draw your own conclusions.
That said, within the synced data, there is a section that catches your eye.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Nirvana and the Workers: Decades of Cooperation and Conflict. The Formation and Current State of Drifter Camp and Rustfire. ...Heh. You tucked individual biographies in here too? What is this, Lives of the "Saviors"?

They're her notes from the fieldwork she's just conducted, so much of it is still unorganized. Yet, you find yourself flipping through them anyway, chapter by chapter, page by page. When you finally come back to yourself and stop, it's nearly daybreak already.
[Enter Flashback]

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: You may not have ambition. But everyone has something they refuse to compromise on. Something they'll protect at any cost.

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: You don't want BR-003 falling into the Underground's hands. So... what's the harm in working with me?
Outside the window, the first light of dawn is breaking. BR-003 remains out of sight, yet the weight of that colossal presence high above pressed down on you all the same.

They built such a facility primarily as a deterrent. But perhaps, too, there are those who hope to use it to shield the people below. Whatever the case, until you witness it for yourself, you will never see anything but its phantom.
And so, you finally make your choice.

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: Your application has been approved. You'll be boarding BR-003 shortly. That said, given the sensitivity of the matter, I will be accompanying you. Is that acceptable, Chief?

steps.speaker: Option
options: I've accepted plenty of things already.

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: You're growing more mature by the day. It's rather heartening to see.

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: Hello, Chief of MBCC. It seems you've reached a decision.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Cooperation aside, I'll support your safety inspection and provide a responsible assessment. Beyond that, I can't promise anything.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: But I imagine that's good enough for you, Director.

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: Quite enough. Thank you for your cooperation, Chief. Then, in return...

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: Your security clearance has been granted. Welcome to the BR-003 Observation Hub.

May 20, N.F. 116, 11:00 AM
2,800 Meters above DisCity
Ring Research Institute BR-003 Observation Hub
